record.original_question: Can the McKay correspondence be generalized at the level of derived categories to the wild case?

evidence.quote: Problem 12.1. Generalize the McKay correspondence at the level of derived categories as studied in [KV00, BKR01] to the wild case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $G \subset \mathrm{GL}(V)$ be a finite subgroup whose order is divisible by $p$ (the "wild" case). Let $X = V/G$ denote the quotient variety, and let $Y \to X$ be a crepant resolution of singularities (when one exists). In characteristic zero (the tame case), the classical derived McKay correspondence asserts an equivalence of triangulated categories
$$ D^b(\mathrm{Coh}\, Y) \;\simeq\; D^b(\mathrm{Coh}^G V) $$
between the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $Y$ and the bounded derived category of $G$-equivariant coherent sheaves on $V$ (as established for finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with $n\le 3$ via the Hilbert scheme of $G$-clusters).

Problem: Formulate and prove an analogue of this derived equivalence in the wild case. Note that the naive statement above cannot hold as written, because in the wild case the category $\mathrm{Coh}^G V$ has infinite global dimension. The task is to identify the correct categorical replacement (for one or both sides) and establish a derived-categorical McKay correspondence valid when $p \mid |G|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in surveys on the wild McKay correspondence. The known obstruction is that the equivariant category $\mathrm{Coh}^G V$ has infinite global dimension when $p \mid |G|$, so the classical Bridgeland–King–Reid/Kapranov–Vasserot equivalence cannot hold verbatim, and an alternative formulation is required. Existing wild McKay correspondences (e.g., via stringy invariants and p-adic measures) operate at the level of invariants, not derived categories, and no derived-category version is known.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the wild McKay correspondence
status_evidence.snippet: Generalize the McKay correspondence at the level of derived categories ... to the wild case.

status_evidence.title: The McKay correspondence as an equivalence of derived categories (Bridgeland–King–Reid)
status_evidence.snippet: Equivalence between derived category of a crepant resolution and the equivariant derived category.
status_evidence.claim: Classical tame statement of the derived McKay correspondence.

status_evidence.title: Wilder McKay correspondences
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations of the wild McKay correspondence via stringy invariants in arbitrary characteristic.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made on invariant-level wild McKay correspondences, not on derived categories.
